title: Integral exchange after base change to a geometric point
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field and $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. For any Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with horizontal maps $g':X'\to X$ and $s$ and vertical maps $f':X'\to\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ and $f$, the canonical exchange component [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] $s^* f_*F\to f'_*g'^*F$ is an isomorphism. No torsion, finite-type, surjectivity or residue-field algebraicity hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0EYP (integral direct-image base change); strict-henselian proof via Tags 03Q9, 09XK, 09ZH and 0A3I

proof.text: Work over an affine open of Y containing the image of s. The integral morphism is affine and qcqs, and its strict-henselian base change is Spec B with B integral over A, where A is the strict henselization at s. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-pushforward-stalk-strict-henselization], the direct-image stalk is sections on Spec B, with every neighbourhood germ sent to its restriction.

Let m be the maximal ideal of A. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-over-henselian-pair], (B,mB) is henselian. Restriction from Spec B to Spec(B/mB) is an isomorphism by the affine special case of [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-degree-zero]: apply its proper morphism hypothesis to the identity of Spec B, not to f. The separably closed residue field kappa of A embeds in Omega. The fibre X' is Spec(B/mB) base changed along kappa -> Omega, and [lem-weil-pbc-sections-base-field-extension] shows that this further restriction is bijective.

At the identity point of Spec Omega, [lemma-openclosed-stalk-upperstar] identifies the source stalk with (f_*F)_s. The terminal-object germ isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk] identifies the target stalk with sections of g'^*F on X'. Expand [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] on a section over a pointed neighbourhood V: the adjunction unit pulls it to X' times_SpecOmega (Spec Omega times_Y V), the square identifies the iterated pullback, and the counit restricts to X'. Hence this is exactly the composite canonical restriction of steps 1 and 2. It is therefore bijective on the identity-point stalk. Forgetting module structure reflects isomorphisms; [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] gives the exchange isomorphism over Spec Omega.
